news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire health and social care partnership running down reserves to cover funding shortfall
news_drafts.lead: The Health and Social Care Partnership serving East Dunbartonshire has depleted nearly a third of its general reserves in a single year to bridge a funding gap, with savings targets falling far short of what is needed. The partnership achieved only 39 per cent of its 2026/27 savings programme by month 4, a shortfall it is covering by drawing down £8.192m from reserves. General contingency reserves have fallen from £3.955m to a projected £1.290m by March 2027. The partnership explicitly warns that continued reliance on reserve drawdowns to balance budgets "may be compromised" its financial sustainability. The financial strain has forced service access restrictions: charges are rising, eligibility criteria tightening and waiting lists extending. A 3.5 per cent pay uplift for staff was approved with no corresponding funding, adding to the pressure. The partnership carried forward £3.036m in unachieved savings from previous years, which must still be realised alongside current targets.
news_drafts.paper_title: Item 14. Hospital Discharge Delays; Performance and Assurance

news_drafts.headline: East Dunbartonshire underlying borrowing need to reach £785m by 2028/29, cash reserves to fall to £1.7m
news_drafts.lead: East Dunbartonshire's underlying borrowing need, the total the council has spent on long-lived assets it has not yet paid for, will grow by 39 per cent over three years to £785m by 2028/29, according to the council's treasury management strategy. The council is currently using cash balances to bridge the gap between what it owes and what it needs to borrow. However, that buffer will shrink by 94 per cent, from £27.6m to £1.7m by 2028/29, as capital spending on housing and other programmes accelerates. Once reserves are exhausted, the council will need to borrow for all new capital expenditure. The forecast reflects a sharp increase in housing investment, with Housing Revenue Account capital spending peaking at £86.4m in 2027/28, more than five times the £16m spent in 2024/25.

findings.paper_title: HOUSING CAPITAL PROGRAMME 2026-27: PERIOD 5 MONITORING REPORT
findings.headline: Cyclical windows and external doors replacement to recommence once a contractor is appointed, expected by end of October 2026
findings.detail: Priority replacements continue on a one-off basis through competitive tendering. A revised procurement arrangement for cyclical replacement is being evaluated, and the paper expects a contractor to be appointed by the end of October 2026, after which cyclical replacement will restart.
findings.matters: A procurement gap in a recurring stock investment line affects the planned spend profile and the forecast for the year.
findings.figures: No cost stated in this paper
findings.quote: a contractor expected to be appointed by the end of October 2026

findings.paper_title: HOUSING CAPITAL PROGRAMME 2026-27: PERIOD 5 MONITORING REPORT
findings.headline: Council reports a close to 100% record of properties with an Electrical Installation Condition Report in the last 5 years
findings.detail: The paper says significant progress was made in 2025/26 surveying properties with no previous electrical inspection history. It states that five-yearly renewals continue to be a strategic priority and that the Council now benefits from this record.
findings.matters: Compliance records of this kind are a stated condition of the housing asset base and are relevant to the Council's regulatory and asset management position.
findings.figures: Close to 100% of properties with an EICR in the last 5 years
findings.quote: the Council now benefits from a close to 100% record of properties having had an EICR in the last 5 years

findings.paper_title: HOUSING CAPITAL PROGRAMME 2026-27: PERIOD 5 MONITORING REPORT
findings.headline: Former Campsie View School, Lenzie project paused pending a Community Asset Transfer appeal due at Council in December
findings.detail: Council considered the Stage 2 report in June 2026 and opted to pause the project. The initial Community Asset Transfer application by the Lenzie Community Development Trust was rejected by Committee, and the applicant has appealed. The project stays paused until the CAT process is exhausted.
findings.matters: A paused scheme with no restart date is a delivery risk and a possible change to the programme forecast, and the decision depends on a December Council decision.
findings.figures: No cost stated in this paper
findings.quote: have opted to pause the project, pending the outcome of a Community Asset Transfer (CAT) application

findings.paper_title: HOUSING CAPITAL PROGRAMME 2026-27: PERIOD 5 MONITORING REPORT
findings.headline: Former Milngavie Primary janitors house proposed for transfer from the General Revenue Account to the HRA at market value
findings.detail: The property was used until recently for temporary homeless accommodation, and the service no longer requires it. The Committee is asked to approve the transfer at market value, with the price to be confirmed on receipt of a valuation and home report. Funding will come from external funding, borrowing or reprogramming, with the preferred model to be confirmed in the next report.
findings.matters: An intra-council transfer at market value moves an asset between accounts and adds a purchase cost that will need funding, which is a treasury question for both the General Fund and the HRA.
findings.figures: No price stated; to be confirmed on valuation
findings.quote: transferred from the General Revenue Account to the Housing Revenue Account at market value

findings.paper_title: HOUSING CAPITAL PROGRAMME 2026-27: PERIOD 5 MONITORING REPORT
findings.headline: Milngavie Police Station acquisition to be met through additional HRA prudential borrowing and/or reprofiled in-year expenditure
findings.detail: The Committee approved the acquisition of the former Milngavie Police Station site in September 2026, and missives are being progressed with Police Scotland. The paper says the cost will be met through either additional prudential borrowing in the Housing Revenue Account or reprofiling of other planned expenditure, with the preferred model to be confirmed in the next report.
findings.matters: The acquisition adds either new HRA borrowing or a reprofiling of other works, and the paper does not yet state which, so the borrowing position is not settled.
findings.figures: No acquisition cost stated in this paper
findings.quote: will be met through either additional prudential borrowing in the Housing Revenue Account and/or through the reprofiling
